insights.title: Your aortic root is wider than expected for your size
insights.found: Echocardiogram on 22 Jul 2026: aortic root 43 mm at the sinuses, Z-score +3.1; ascending aorta 34 mm; mild mitral valve prolapse without leakage. You take losartan 50 mg daily since 1 Aug 2026 for this.
insights.why: A Z-score compares your aorta with people of your body size; +3.1 is well above average.
insights.means: Your clinic is treating the widening and following it with scans. Your blood pressure was 116/64.
insights.do: Keep your scheduled scans and keep taking losartan.
insights.expected: Your clinic sees any change early.
insights.helps: The most important thing your clinic is watching.

insights.title: Your FBN1 variant is of uncertain significance
insights.found: Exome sequencing found one copy of FBN1 c.4270C>G (p.Pro1424Ala). It is reported as a variant of uncertain significance; ClinVar (VCV000042355) lists conflicting classifications.
insights.why: Only you were sequenced (no parents), so the variant cannot yet be traced through your family.
insights.means: A variant of uncertain significance cannot by itself confirm or rule out a diagnosis. Your clinic asked whether your features support reclassifying it.
insights.do: Ask your genetics team whether testing relatives could help classify it.
insights.expected: A clearer answer for you and your family.

insights.title: Your body features have been recorded and matched
insights.found: Recorded: tall stature (196 cm), arm span 203 cm (ratio 1.04), long fingers, both lenses displaced, aortic root widening, sunken chest, stretch marks, short-sightedness and flexible joints.
insights.why: Our disease stage matched these signs against known conditions.
insights.means: The closest computer matches were isolated ectopia lentis, a familial thoracic aortic aneurysm type, MASS syndrome and Loeys-Dietz syndrome. This is pattern matching, not a diagnosis; Marfan syndrome is recorded as suspected by your clinic.
insights.do: Your clinic weighs these with the formal criteria.

insights.title: Your father's sudden death matters for your care
insights.found: Your father died suddenly at 41, with an aortic dissection suspected. Your paternal aunt is reported to be tall with lens dislocation (unconfirmed).
insights.why: Family history is part of how your clinic assesses the aorta and the variant.
insights.means: It makes careful follow-up and family assessment especially relevant.
insights.do: Share any confirmed family records with your clinic.
insights.expected: A stronger basis for your family's care.

insights.title: Both of your lenses are displaced
insights.found: Slit-lamp examination on 30 Jun 2026: both lenses displaced upwards and outwards (superotemporal subluxation). You are also short-sighted.
insights.why: Displaced lenses are one of the features your clinic records.

insights.title: Your homocysteine is normal
insights.found: Homocysteine 9.8 umol/L on 16 Oct 2026, inside the lab's range of 5-15.
insights.why: It was requested to help exclude homocystinuria, a condition that can also displace the lenses.
insights.means: A normal result fits with that request.

insights.title: Your activity advice is on record
insights.found: You swim recreationally and have been advised to avoid competitive and isometric sports.
insights.why: This advice is in your clinic record.
insights.means: Your clinic sets what is safe for your aorta.
insights.do: Ask your clinic before starting any new sport.

ask.a: Your clinic records Marfan syndrome as suspected, not confirmed. You have aortic root widening (Z +3.1) and displaced lenses, and an FBN1 variant of uncertain significance. Whether this meets the formal criteria is your clinic's call.

It means the evidence is not enough to call your FBN1 variant (c.4270C>G) disease-causing or harmless. ClinVar lists conflicting classifications for it. More evidence, for example from relatives, can change that.
Your aortic root was 43 mm at the sinuses on 22 Jul 2026, a Z-score of +3.1 for your body size; the ascending aorta was 34 mm.
Your record says losartan 50 mg daily was started on 1 Aug 2026 for aortic root widening.
Your father died suddenly at 41 with a suspected aortic dissection, and your aunt is reported to have lens dislocation. Only you were sequenced; ask your genetics team about testing relatives.
Your clinic advised recreational swimming and avoiding competitive and isometric sports. Ask before starting anything new.

Computer matching of your features ranked isolated ectopia lentis, a familial thoracic aortic aneurysm type, MASS syndrome and Loeys-Dietz syndrome among the closest. Pattern matching only. Your homocysteine was normal, which makes homocystinuria less likely.
Both lenses are displaced upwards and outwards (seen on 30 Jun 2026), and you are short-sighted. Your eye team follows this.

ask.q: What did the drug discovery research find?
ask.a: It found 25 biological targets (the portal lists the first 12), including FBN1 and the TGF-beta receptors TGFBR1 and TGFBR2, and profiled 367 known compounds. No docking was run. Research only, not treatment.

ask.q: Why did no rule fire for me?
ask.a: Our rule library checked 75 rules; none fired because your few lab results are in range and no rule covers aortic size or gene variants. Your cards come from your clinic record instead.
